neighbours.label: the head in a head gesture of reply (shaking or nodding the head), also on 'shook' itself as it anticipates 'head'
fire: Asked whether she had seen the letter, Mara slowly shook her head.
The old fisherman just shook his head at the tourists on the pier.
When the waiter offered dessert, both children shook their heads.
Tom listened to the plan and nodded his head in agreement.
The referee kept shaking his head as the players argued.
My mother looked at the broken vase and shook her head sadly.
Hearing the price, the farmer shook his head and turned away.
Everyone in the jury box nodded their heads at the closing words.
quiet: Asked whether she had seen the letter, Mara slowly covered her head.
The old fisherman just bumped his head on the beam over the pier.
When the waiter offered dessert, both children wiped their mouths.
Tom listened to the plan and rubbed his head with a towel.
The referee kept touching his head where the ball had hit him.
My mother looked at the broken vase and held her head in pain.
Hearing the price, the farmer took off his hat and turned away.
Everyone in the jury box turned their heads toward the door.
